title: How apprenticeships are developing stronger dental teams across England
html:
Poultec Training explores the benefits of apprenticeships in the dental sector, from dental nurses to administrators and support staff.

Recruiting, developing and retaining skilled people remains a priority for many dental practices. From clinical care to front-of-house support, every member of the team contributes to the patient experience and the smooth running of the practice.

For employers, the challenge is not only finding the right people, but keeping them, developing them and creating clear routes for progression. Apprenticeship training can support this by providing a structured and funded way to train new recruits, develop existing staff, and build skills across the whole practice team.

Training trainee dental nurses

The dental nurse apprenticeship remains one of the most recognised apprenticeship routes within dentistry. For practices struggling to recruit qualified dental nurses, it offers a practical alternative to relying only on already-qualified candidates.

Through the Level 3 dental nurse apprenticeship, trainee dental nurses can work in practice while developing skills in areas such as chairside support, patient care, infection control, radiography, health and safety, and professional practice.

For employers, learners can be trained around the practice’s own systems, standards and approach to patient care from the beginning. For learners, it provides a clear route into dental nursing, combining workplace experience with recognised training.

The apprenticeship supports trainee dental nurses to gain the knowledge, skills and qualification needed to apply to the General Dental Council (GDC) for professional registration as a dental nurse. The GDC currently requires all new trainee dental nurses to start a recognised training programme within 12 months of starting work. For practices, this makes early planning and choosing the right training route even more important.

Developing the wider dental team

While dental nurse training is a vital part of workforce development, apprenticeships can support much more than clinical roles alone.

Receptionists, administrators and patient support staff are often the first point of contact for patients. Their communication, organisation and confidence can influence patient experience, appointment flow, and practice efficiency.

A dental receptionist apprenticeship can support front-of-house staff to develop skills in patient communication, appointment booking, customer service, administration and handling enquiries professionally.

An apprenticeship for dental administrators can help staff build stronger skills in records, processes, communication, coordination and wider practice support. This can be useful for team members taking on more responsibility or supporting areas such as compliance, patient coordination or practice administration.

By developing non-clinical staff, practices can improve efficiency, reduce pressure on colleagues, and support a better experience for patients.

Progression for registered dental nurses

Retaining dental nurses is just as important as recruiting new ones. Many registered dental nurses are keen to continue developing once they are qualified. Without clear development routes, practices risk losing skilled team members who want to progress.

The Level 4 Oral Health Practitioner apprenticeship can support GDC-registered dental nurses to develop prevention-focused skills including oral health education, patient-centred care and oral and general health improvement.

For practices, this can help strengthen prevention, patient education and wider clinical support. For dental nurses, it offers a structured progression route that allows them to continue working while developing new skills and confidence.

Making apprenticeships work in practice

One of the main benefits of apprenticeship training is that it is work-based. Learners gain new knowledge and skills while continuing their role in the practice, supported by their employer and training provider.

Funding may also be available, with up to 100% of training and assessment costs covered depending on eligibility. This can help practices train new recruits and existing employees in a cost-effective way.

Successful apprenticeship delivery relies on the right support. Practices need clear communication, funding guidance and a provider that understands the pace and pressures of a dental environment.

Poultec Training works with dental practices across England to deliver apprenticeship training shaped around the needs of each practice. Poultec offers dental apprenticeships to support both clinical and non-clinical roles, from trainee dental nurses and dental receptionists to administrators and oral health practitioner progression for registered dental nurses. Employers and learners are supported throughout the apprenticeship journey.

‘Dental practices are built around people,’ said Ben Gaskins, head of business development at Poultec Training. ‘Apprenticeships can help practices invest in their team, create progression routes and develop skills that support both staff and patients.’

For dental practices, apprenticeships are more than a recruitment route. Used well, they can support retention, progression and long-term workforce planning across the whole team.
